title: Beat-Synchronous Tokenization for ECG Transformers
abstract: arXiv:2608.30367v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Transformer-based electrocardiogram (ECG) models commonly tokenize waveforms into fixed temporal patches. Though convenient, fixed patching can split heartbeat structures across token boundaries. We study beat-synchronous tokenization as a physiologically grounded alternative, comparing fixed patches with three beat-aligned strategies: resampled beats, adaptive pooled beats, and resampled beats augmented with R--R interval information. Experiments span two settings: 10-second 12-lead diagnostic classification on PTB-XL after MIMIC-IV-ECG masked pretraining, and 60-second single-lead rhythm classification on Icentia11k after patient-level contrastive pretraining. On PTB-XL, resampled beat tokens achieve the highest mean macro Area Under the ROC Curve (AUROC; 0.8945) and nearly match the best fixed-patch macro Area Under the Precision-Recall Curve (AUPRC; 0.7414), reducing average sequence length from 100 to 11.2 tokens. translated_title: 面向心电图Transformer的心拍同步分词方法

tldr: 提出以心拍为单位的同步分词策略替代固定时间分块，使心电图Transformer在诊断与心律分类性能相当或更优的同时，将序列长度从100个标记大幅压缩至约11个。
en_tdlr: Beat-synchronous tokenization matches or exceeds fixed patching for ECG transformers across diagnostic and rhythm classification tasks, while reducing sequence length from 100 to about 11 tokens.
